resources.string: A schematic overhead view of horizontal adduction at the shoulder. It isolates the sweep and does not show full shoulder mechanics or measure range of motion.
The clavicular fibers start at the inner clavicle. The sternocostal fibers start at the sternum and nearby costal cartilages.
The fan narrows into a tendon on the outer lip of the groove between the tubercles of the upper humerus.
With the upper arm raised out to the side, pectoralis major contributes to its forward sweep at the shoulder.
The humerus continues across the front of the chest. The humeral attachment travels with the bone while the chest origins stay in place in this view.
The diagram reverses the sweep to compare the positions. It does not show which muscles produce the return.
Kuechle et al.: horizontal flexion at the shoulder
A schematic view from behind and to the side. It separates shoulder extension and adduction for comparison and does not measure range of motion.
A broad sheet on the back
Latissimus dorsi arises from the lower thoracic spine, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, and lower ribs.
The muscle narrows near the back of the armpit. Its tendon curves around teres major to attach to the floor of the groove at the front of the upper humerus.
From a position in front and to the side, the upper arm moves backward relative to the trunk. Latissimus dorsi contributes to shoulder extension.
The upper arm then moves closer to the side of the trunk. Latissimus dorsi also contributes to shoulder adduction.
The diagram retraces both parts of the path. This reversal compares poses without modeling the muscles that produce the return.
